Supported Workflows & Simulation Limitations Expand
Supported Sabre GDS Training Workflows
  • Flight availability search (120NOVDACDXB¥BG) with live carrier filtering and seat sell (01Y1).
  • Complete PNR creation across 6 independent work areas (A–F) with mandatory PRINT elements and 6-character record locators.
  • APIS passport, visa, address, and IATA Resolution 830d passenger contact entries (3DOCS, 3DOCO, 3DOCA, 3CTCM, 3CTCE).
  • Itinerary pricing (WP, WPNCB, PQ), E-Ticket issuance (W¥PQ1...), same-day void (WV2), automated refund quote (WFRA), refund execution (WFRA/REF / WFR), and automated reissue (WFRF ➔ *PQR ➔ W¥PQR1).
Simulation Scope & Boundaries
  • Operates entirely as a client-side educational simulator; no real airline inventory or BSP settlement is modified.
  • Fares, taxes (BD/UT/E5/OW), and 7% commission defaults represent a configured Bangladesh BSP training scenario and vary by carrier in live production.
  • Generated E-Ticket receipts and completion certificates are training records only and do not constitute an IATA or Sabre license.

15-Minute Practical Sabre GDS Exam

Starts an isolated exam workspace (/exams/session/:attemptId) separate from Free Practice. The timer begins only when you click Start Practical Exam below.

Required Exam Tasks (5 Checkpoints — 20% Each):
  1. Search & sell a confirmed flight segment (120NOVDACDXB¥BG ➔ 01Y1).
  2. Add passenger name, agency phone, ticketing time limit, and received-from (-, 9, 7TAW/, 6).
  3. End and retrieve PNR (ER) to generate a 6-character record locator.
  4. Add mandatory APIS passport and IATA Res 830d contact SSRs (3DOCS, 3CTCM, 3CTCE) and store fare (WP ➔ PQ).
  5. Issue the 13-digit electronic ticket (W¥PQ1N1.1¥ABG¥FINVAGT¥KP7¥ETR¥ER).

Scenario Assumptions, Applicable Scope & Sources

Last Reviewed: November 2026

Applicable Scope: Commission rates, tax codes, and fare penalties are not universal; they depend on the point of sale, validating carrier, and fare basis. All calculations in this simulator represent a configured Bangladesh BSP training scenario:

  • Commission Default: 7% (KP7) is used as the training default for published fares (KP0 for net/reissued fares).
  • Tax Breakdown: Sample tax calculations include Bangladesh Embarkation Fee (BD BDT 500), Travel Tax (UT), Airport Development Fee (E5), and Security Fee (OW).

Reference Standards:

  • Automated Refunds & Exchanges: Sabre Red 360 Automated Refunds (WFRA<13-digit TKT> quote display & WFRA<13-digit TKT>/REF refund execution, ATPCO Category 33) and Automated Exchanges (WFRF / *PQR / W¥PQR1, ATPCO Category 31).
  • IATA Resolutions: IATA Resolution 850m (Agency Debit Memo 15-day dispute window) and IATA Resolution 830d (SSR CTCM / SSR CTCE passenger contact requirement).
About & Disclaimer

About MY AIR ACADEMY

Independent browser-based training environment for travel agency trainees and aviation students.

MY AIR ACADEMY provides a distraction-free Sabre GDS command-line simulator designed to help learners practise flight availability, PNR creation, APIS compliance, fare pricing, electronic ticketing, automated refunds (WFRA), and automated reissues (WFRF) at their own pace.

Simulation Policy & Non-Affiliation Notice: This website is an independent educational simulator. No real airline seats are held, no live PNRs are transmitted to airline hosts, and no real electronic tickets or financial transactions are issued. MY AIR ACADEMY is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sabre Corporation or IATA.

IATA World Traffic Conference Areas (TC1, TC2 & TC3 Master Map)

Official IATA geographical division of the world into Western Hemisphere (Area 1) and Eastern Hemisphere (Areas 2 & 3)

ALL 3 AREAS
TC1 — Traffic Conference Area 1 (Western Hemisphere)
  • North America: USA (incl. Alaska & Hawaii), Canada, Mexico, Greenland (GOH).
  • Central America: Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica.
  • Caribbean Islands: Bahamas, Bermuda, Cuba, Jamaica, Haiti, Dominican Rep., Trinidad, Aruba.
  • South America: Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Venezuela, Panama, Ecuador, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay.
TC2 — Traffic Conference Area 2 (Europe, Middle East, Africa)
  • Europe: All EU/UK/Schengen states, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Turkey (IST/ANK), Russia West of Urals (MOW/LED), Ukraine, Caucasus (GE, AZ, AM), plus Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia.
  • Middle East: Saudi Arabia (JED/RUH), UAE (DXB/AUH), Qatar (DOH), Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Jordan, Lebanon, Iraq, Iran, Egypt (CAI), Sudan.
  • Africa: Central, Eastern, Southern, Western Africa & Indian Ocean Islands (Mauritius, Seychelles).
TC3 — Traffic Conference Area 3 (Asia & Oceania)
  • South Asian Subcontinent (SASC): Bangladesh (DAC/CGP/ZYL), India (DEL/BOM/CCU), Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Maldives, Bhutan, Afghanistan.
  • South East Asia (SEA): Singapore (SIN), Thailand (BKK), Malaysia (KUL), Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Central Asia & Russia East of Urals.
  • Japan / Korea: Japan (TYO/OSA), South Korea (SEL), North Korea (FNJ).
  • South West Pacific (SWP): Australia (SYD/MEL/CBR), New Zealand (AKL/WLG), Fiji, PNG, Tahiti, Samoa, Guam.

              IATA ADM Shield & BSPlink Audit Hub — 12 Official Causes of Agency Debit Memos & Prevention
            

            

              Interactive guide to Sabre GDS commands that trigger Airline ADMs, penalty structures, and the 15-day IATA Resolution 850m BSPlink dispute workflow
            

          

        

        

          
        

      


      
      

        

          
          
          
        

        

          
        

      


      
      

        
        

          

            
WHAT IS AN ADM?

            
Agency Debit Memo

            
An accounting debit raised by an airline via IATA BSPlink to collect underpaid fares, taxes, or booking abuse penalties from an agency.

          

          

            
DISPUTE WINDOW (RES 850m)

            
15 Days Dispute Window

            
Under IATA Resolution 850m, agencies have 15 days from issuance to dispute an ADM in BSPlink before billing; airlines have 60 days to resolve.

          

          

            
MAX ISSUANCE LIMIT

            
9 Months Post-Travel Limit

            
Airlines may only process an ADM through BSP within 9 months of the final travel date of the ticketed itinerary.
